speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning signs of a systemic illness. To begin our workup, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool caliber recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those systemic symptoms. Given the weight loss, night sweats, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, could you tell me if you have noticed any blood in your stool or a change in stool caliber?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of the supraclavicular node as "fixed" is highly concerning for malignancy. To help us distinguish between a gastrointestinal primary and lymphoma, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing food recently, and would you agree to a test for HIV status?
